questions.question: Why does a compass needle get deflected when brought near a bar magnet?
answer_steps: A compass needle is itself a small magnet.
Near a bar magnet it experiences a force in the magnet's magnetic field, so it turns (attraction of unlike poles, repulsion of like poles).

questions.question: Draw magnetic field lines around a bar magnet.
answer_steps: Draw closed curves that leave the north pole and enter the south pole outside the magnet, with arrows from N to S.
Draw the lines crowded near the poles and spread out away from them; no two lines cross.

questions.question: List the properties of magnetic field lines.
answer_steps: Outside a magnet they go from the north pole to the south pole; inside, from south to north: they are closed curves.
They are crowded where the field is strong and spread out where it is weak.
No two field lines intersect.

questions.question: Why don't two magnetic field lines intersect each other?
answer_steps: At the point of intersection a compass needle would have to point in two directions at once.
This is impossible, because the field has only one direction at any point.

questions.question: Consider a circular loop of wire lying in the plane of the table. Let the current pass through the loop clockwise. Apply the right-hand rule to find out the direction of the magnetic field inside and outside the loop.
answer_steps: Hold each part of the loop in the right hand with the thumb along the clockwise current.
Inside the loop, the curled fingers point downward: the field is into the table.
Outside the loop, the field points upward: out of the table.

questions.question: The magnetic field in a given region is uniform. Draw a diagram to represent it.
answer_steps: Draw equally spaced, parallel straight lines.
Put arrows all pointing the same way, to show the same strength and direction everywhere.

questions.question: Which of the following property of a proton can change while it moves freely in a magnetic field? (There may be more than one correct answer.)
questions.explanation: The magnetic force is perpendicular to the motion, so it changes the direction (velocity, momentum) but not the speed or the mass.
option_feedback: Correct!
Mass does not change.
The force is perpendicular, so the speed stays the same.
Neither changes.

questions.question: In Activity 12.7, how do we think the displacement of rod AB will be affected if (i) current in rod AB is increased; (ii) a stronger horse-shoe magnet is used; and (iii) length of the rod AB is increased?
answer_steps: (i) The displacement increases, because the force increases with the current.
(ii) The displacement increases, because the force increases with the strength of the field.
(iii) The displacement increases, because a longer rod in the field feels a larger force.

questions.question: A positively-charged particle (alpha-particle) projected towards west is deflected towards north by a magnetic field. The direction of magnetic field is
questions.explanation: Fleming's left-hand rule: current (middle finger) west, force (thumb) north, so the field (forefinger) points upward.
option_feedback: Use Fleming's left-hand rule with current west and force north.
That is along the motion, giving no force.
That would push it south.
Correct!

questions.question: Name two safety measures commonly used in electric circuits and appliances.
answer_steps: An electric fuse (or a miniature circuit breaker) in series with the live wire.
Earthing: an earth wire connecting the metal body of an appliance to the ground.

questions.question: An electric oven of 2 kW power rating is operated in a domestic electric circuit (220 V) that has a current rating of 5 A. What result do you expect? Explain.
answer_steps: $I = \dfrac{P}{V} = \dfrac{2000}{220} \approx 9.1$ A
This is more than the 5 A rating, so the circuit is overloaded and the fuse will blow (melt), cutting off the supply.

questions.question: What precaution should be taken to avoid the overloading of domestic electric circuits?
answer_steps: Do not connect too many appliances to a single socket at the same time.
Use appliances whose current is within the rating of the circuit (heavy appliances on the 15 A circuit), and use a fuse or MCB of the correct rating.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the magnetic field near a long straight wire?
options: The field consists of straight lines perpendicular to the wire.
The field consists of straight lines parallel to the wire.
The field consists of radial lines originating from the wire.
The field consists of concentric circles centred on the wire.
questions.explanation: The field lines are concentric circles around the wire.
option_feedback: The lines go round the wire.
The lines go round the wire.
The lines are circles, not radial.
Correct!

questions.question: At the time of short circuit, the current in the circuit
questions.explanation: The resistance becomes nearly zero, so the current becomes very large.
option_feedback: The resistance falls, so the current rises.
It rises sharply.
Correct!
It rises sharply.

questions.question: State whether the following statement is true or false: The field at the centre of a long circular coil carrying current will be parallel straight lines.
questions.explanation: Near the centre of a current-carrying circular coil, the field lines are straight and parallel.
option_feedback: Correct! Near the centre of a current-carrying circular coil, the field lines are straight and parallel.
Not quite. Near the centre of a current-carrying circular coil, the field lines are straight and parallel.

questions.question: State whether the following statement is true or false: A wire with a green insulation is usually the live wire of an electric supply.
questions.explanation: The green wire is the earth wire; the live wire has red insulation.
option_feedback: Not quite. The green wire is the earth wire; the live wire has red insulation.
Correct! The green wire is the earth wire; the live wire has red insulation.

questions.question: List two methods of producing magnetic fields.
answer_steps: Using a permanent magnet, such as a bar magnet.
Passing an electric current through a conductor: a straight wire, a circular loop or a solenoid (electromagnet).

questions.question: When is the force experienced by a current–carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field largest?
answer_steps: When the direction of the current is perpendicular to the magnetic field.
(It is zero when the current is parallel to the field.)

questions.question: Imagine that you are sitting in a chamber with your back to one wall. An electron beam, moving horizontally from back wall towards the front wall, is deflected by a strong magnetic field to your right side. What is the direction of magnetic field?
answer_steps: The electrons move towards the front wall, so the current is towards the back wall; the force is to the right.
By Fleming's left-hand rule, the magnetic field is vertically downward.

questions.question: State the rule to determine the direction of a (i) magnetic field produced around a straight conductor-carrying current, (ii) force experienced by a current-carrying straight conductor placed in a magnetic field which is perpendicular to it, and (iii) current induced in a coil due to its rotation in a magnetic field.
answer_steps: (i) Right-hand thumb rule: hold the conductor in the right hand with the thumb along the current; the curled fingers give the direction of the field.
(ii) Fleming's left-hand rule: stretch the thumb, forefinger and middle finger of the left hand at right angles; forefinger = field, middle finger = current, thumb = force.
(iii) Fleming's right-hand rule: with the right hand, forefinger = field, thumb = motion of the conductor, middle finger = induced current.

questions.question: When does an electric short circuit occur?
answer_steps: When the live wire and the neutral wire come in direct contact, for example when the insulation is damaged or an appliance is faulty.
The resistance becomes nearly zero, and the current increases heavily.

questions.question: What is the function of an earth wire? Why is it necessary to earth metallic appliances?
answer_steps: The earth wire provides a low-resistance path from the metal body of an appliance to the ground.
If the live wire touches the metal body, the leaking current flows to the earth, so the user does not get a severe electric shock.

questions.question:
Magnetic field lines around a bar magnet are shown in a diagram: point X is close to a pole, where the lines are crowded, and point Y is farther away, where the lines are spread out. A student makes a statement that the magnetic field at X is stronger than at Y.

(i) Explain with reason if the student's claim is correct.

(ii) Also redraw the diagram and mark the direction of magnetic field lines.
answer_steps: (i) The claim is correct: the closeness of the field lines shows the strength of the field.
The lines are more crowded at X (near the pole) than at Y, so the field at X is stronger.
(ii) Arrows on the field lines should go from the north pole to the south pole outside the magnet.

questions.question: Write down the characteristics of field lines around a bar magnet.
answer_steps: They go from the north pole to the south pole outside the magnet and form closed curves.
They are crowded near the poles where the field is strong, and no two lines intersect.

questions.question: Explain the right-hand thumb rule.
answer_steps: Imagine holding a current-carrying straight conductor in your right hand, with the thumb pointing in the direction of the current.
Then the fingers wrapped around the conductor give the direction of the magnetic field lines.

questions.question:
(a) Draw a schematic diagram of domestic electric circuit.

(b) What is the importance of fuse and earth wire in domestic electric circuit?
answer_steps: (a) Mains (live, neutral, earth) → meter → main fuse → distribution box → separate circuits (15 A and 5 A), with appliances connected in parallel, each with its own switch; the earth wire goes to every metal body.
(b) Fuse: it melts and breaks the circuit when the current becomes too large (short circuit or overloading), preventing damage to appliances and fire.
Earth wire: it carries any leaking current from the metal body of an appliance to the ground, protecting the user from a severe shock.

questions.question: Explain: Solenoid
answer_steps: A solenoid is a coil of many circular turns of insulated copper wire wrapped closely in the shape of a cylinder.
When current flows, its field is like that of a bar magnet, and the field inside is uniform; with a soft iron core it becomes an electromagnet.

questions.question: Explain Fleming's left-hand rule.
answer_steps: Stretch the thumb, forefinger and middle finger of the left hand so that they are mutually perpendicular.
If the forefinger points along the magnetic field and the middle finger along the current, the thumb gives the direction of the force (motion) on the conductor.

questions.question:
(a) List the properties of magnetic field lines.

(b) When does an electric short circuit occur?
answer_steps: (a) They go from the north pole to the south pole outside a magnet and form closed curves; they are crowded where the field is strong.
No two field lines intersect.
(b) When the live wire and the neutral wire come in direct contact; the resistance becomes nearly zero and the current increases heavily.

questions.question: Outside a bar magnet, magnetic field lines go from:
questions.explanation: Outside, from N to S; inside, from S to N.
option_feedback: That is inside the magnet.
They run from pole to pole.
They exist all around the magnet.
Correct!

questions.question: The magnetic field is strongest where the field lines are:
questions.explanation: Crowded lines mean a strong field.
option_feedback: Curvature does not show strength.
Straightness does not show strength.
Correct!
Spread-out lines mean a weak field.

questions.question: The field around a straight wire becomes stronger when:
options: you move away from the wire
questions.explanation: The field increases with current and decreases with distance.
option_feedback: The field weakens with distance.
Correct!
Length does not change the field near it.
Less current, weaker field.

questions.question: A soft iron core inside a solenoid makes it:
questions.explanation: The iron core greatly strengthens the field while the current flows.
option_feedback: Correct!
Soft iron loses magnetism when the current stops.
Iron strengthens the field.
It is not used as a resistor.

questions.question: In Fleming's left-hand rule, the thumb shows the direction of:
questions.explanation: Forefinger = field, middle finger = current, thumb = force.
option_feedback: That is the middle finger.
That is the forefinger.
Voltage is not part of the rule.
Correct!

questions.question: The frequency of AC supply in India is:
questions.explanation: Indian mains supply is 220 V, 50 Hz.
option_feedback: 220 is the voltage.
It changes direction 100 times a second, but the frequency is 50 Hz.
Correct!
That is used in some other countries.

questions.question: The live wire in a domestic circuit usually has insulation of colour:
questions.explanation: Live is red, neutral is black, earth is green.
option_feedback: Not used for live in the NCERT convention.
Correct!
Green is earth.
Black is neutral.

questions.question: Heavy appliances such as a geyser are connected to a circuit of rating:
questions.explanation: Heavy appliances use the 15 A circuit; bulbs and fans use the 5 A circuit.
option_feedback: Correct!
That is for bulbs and fans.
Far too low.
Domestic circuits use 15 A.

questions.question: An advantage of AC over DC is that AC:
options: can be stored in a cell
can be transmitted over long distances without much energy loss
questions.explanation: AC can be sent over long distances with little loss.
option_feedback: That is DC.
Cells store DC.
AC has a frequency of 50 Hz.
Correct!

questions.question: A beam of electrons moving towards the east is equivalent to a current towards the:
questions.explanation: Current is opposite to the motion of electrons.
option_feedback: Current is opposite to electron motion.
The motion is along east-west.
The motion is along east-west.
Correct!

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** Two magnetic field lines never intersect.

**Reason (R):** At any point the magnetic field has only one direction.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Crossing would need two directions at one point: R explains A.
option_feedback: Correct! A is true: field lines never cross. R is true: two directions at one point are impossible.
R does explain A: two directions at one point are impossible.
Check the Reason again: it is true, because two directions at one point are impossible.
Check the Assertion again: it is true, because field lines never cross.

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** A fuse is connected in series with the live wire.

**Reason (R):** A fuse melts and breaks the circuit when the current becomes too large.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Being in series, its melting cuts off the whole supply: R explains A.
option_feedback: Correct! A is true: the fuse is in series with the live wire. R is true: being in series, its melting cuts off the supply.
R does explain A: being in series, its melting cuts off the supply.
Check the Reason again: it is true, because being in series, its melting cuts off the supply.
Check the Assertion again: it is true, because the fuse is in series with the live wire.

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** The metal body of an electric iron is earthed.

**Reason (R):** The earth wire carries current all the time the iron is in use.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.explanation: A is true. R is false: the earth wire carries current only when there is a leakage.
option_feedback: Check the Reason again: it is false, because the earth wire carries current only during a leakage.
Check the Reason again: it is false, because the earth wire carries current only during a leakage.
Correct! A is true: metal bodies are earthed for safety. R is false: the earth wire carries current only during a leakage.
Check the Assertion again: it is true, because metal bodies are earthed for safety.

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** The magnetic field inside a long solenoid is uniform.

**Reason (R):** Inside a solenoid the field lines are parallel straight lines.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Parallel, equally spaced lines mean a uniform field: R explains A.
option_feedback: Correct! A is true: the field inside a solenoid is uniform. R is true: parallel, equally spaced lines mean a uniform field.
R does explain A: parallel, equally spaced lines mean a uniform field.
Check the Reason again: it is true, because parallel, equally spaced lines mean a uniform field.
Check the Assertion again: it is true, because the field inside a solenoid is uniform.

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** The force on a current-carrying conductor is zero when it is parallel to the magnetic field.

**Reason (R):** The force is largest when the conductor is perpendicular to the field.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Both are true, but the maximum at 90° does not explain why the force is zero at 0°.
option_feedback: Both are true, but R is not the reason A is true: the maximum at 90° does not explain the zero at 0°.
Correct! A is true: there is no force when the conductor is along the field. R is true: the maximum at 90° does not explain the zero at 0°.
Check the Reason again: it is true, because the maximum at 90° does not explain the zero at 0°.
Check the Assertion again: it is true, because there is no force when the conductor is along the field.

questions.question: Differentiate between direct current and alternating current.
answer_steps: Direct current (DC) flows in one direction only, for example from a cell.
Alternating current (AC) reverses its direction periodically; in India it has a frequency of 50 Hz.

questions.question: What is overloading? Give two causes.
answer_steps: Overloading is when the current drawn in a circuit becomes more than its rated value.
Causes: too many appliances connected to a single socket; an accidental rise in the supply voltage.

questions.question: Describe the magnetic field produced by a current-carrying solenoid. How can it be used to make an electromagnet?
answer_steps: A current-carrying solenoid produces a field like that of a bar magnet: one end behaves as a north pole and the other as a south pole.
Inside, the field lines are parallel straight lines, so the field is uniform.
Placing a soft iron core inside and passing current makes a strong electromagnet, whose magnetism disappears when the current is switched off.

questions.question: On what factors does the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field depend? How can its direction be reversed?
answer_steps: The force increases with the current, the strength of the magnetic field and the length of the conductor in the field.
It also depends on the angle: it is largest when the conductor is perpendicular to the field.
Its direction is reversed by reversing either the current or the magnetic field.

questions.question: Describe the magnetic field produced by (a) a straight current-carrying wire (b) a circular loop. State the rule used to find its direction, and the factors on which the field of a straight wire depends.
answer_steps: (a) Straight wire: the field lines are concentric circles centred on the wire, in a plane perpendicular to it.
(b) Circular loop: near the centre the field lines are nearly straight and parallel; the field of n turns is n times that of one turn.
Rule: the right-hand thumb rule, with the thumb along the current and the curled fingers showing the field.
The field of a straight wire increases with the current.
It decreases as the distance from the wire increases.

questions.question: Describe a domestic electric circuit. Explain the functions of the live wire, neutral wire, earth wire and fuse. What is a short circuit?
answer_steps: Mains supply at 220 V, 50 Hz enters through the meter and the main fuse; appliances are connected in parallel on 15 A and 5 A circuits, each with its own switch.
Live wire (red) brings the current at 220 V; neutral wire (black) returns it.
Earth wire (green) connects metal bodies to the ground and carries leaking current away, preventing shocks.
Fuse: in series with the live wire, it melts when the current is too large and breaks the circuit.
Short circuit: live and neutral touch directly, the resistance becomes nearly zero, and the current rises heavily.

questions.question:
During Diwali, Aman plugged a heater, an iron and several decorative lights into one multi-plug socket. After some time, the fuse blew and the house went dark. An electrician advised using the 15 A circuit for the heater and the iron.

(i) What is this situation called? (1)

(ii) Why did the fuse blow? (1)

(iii) Why are heavy appliances connected to the 15 A circuit? OR Why is the fuse connected in the live wire and not in the neutral wire? (2)
answer_steps: (i) Overloading.
(ii) The total current drawn became more than the fuse's rating, so the fuse wire heated up and melted.

(iii) Heavy appliances draw a large current; the 15 A circuit has thicker wires and a higher-rated fuse that can carry it safely. OR If the fuse melts in the live wire, the appliance is completely cut off from the high-voltage supply, so it is safe to touch.

questions.question:
In a scrap yard, a crane lifts old cars with a huge electromagnet. When the operator switches off the current, the car drops. Nearby, a compass placed under the crane's cable turned when the current was on.

(i) What does the electromagnet consist of? (1)

(ii) Why does the car drop when the current is switched off? (1)

(iii) Why did the compass turn? OR Give two ways to make the electromagnet stronger. (2)
answer_steps: (i) A solenoid (coil of insulated wire) with a soft iron core.
(ii) The soft iron core loses its magnetism when the current stops.
(iii) The current in the cable produces a magnetic field around it, which exerts a force on the compass needle. OR Increase the current; increase the number of turns of the coil.
